✨ Show a clear error on attempt to include router into itself

Previously discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/11424 with the PR at https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/11425

steps.message:
The issue is that including an `APIRouter` into itself (or causing a circular reference during router inclusion) leads to an infinite loop/hang instead of a clear error. The `include_router` method in `APIRouter` (and `FastAPI`) iterates over the routes of the included router and adds them to itself. If a router is included in itself, any routes already present in that router will be processed recursively or cause a loop when the final app tries to resolve the routes.

FILES: `fastapi/routing.py`:`include_router` (and potentially `fastapi/applications.py`:`include_router`)
CAUSE: Missing check for circular references when including a router into itself.
FIX: Add a check at the beginning of `include_router` to verify if the `router` being included is the same instance as `self`. If so, raise a `FastAPIError` with a message indicating a circular reference.
REPRO: A script that creates an `APIRouter`, adds a route to it, and then calls `router.include_router(router)`, which currently hangs.
TESTS: `tests/test_include_router_defaults_overrides.py` (can add a new test case here).

Plan:
1. Modify `fastapi/routing.py` in `APIRouter.include_router` to check `if router is self: raise FastAPIError("A router cannot include itself")`.
2. Modify `fastapi/applications.py` in `FastAPI.include_router` for consistency if needed, although `FastAPI` is the root. However, `FastAPI` inherits from `APIRouter` (or shares logic), so ensuring the check is in the base `APIRouter.include_router` is key. Wait, `FastAPI` also has its own `include_router` that calls `super().include_router` or similar logic. I will check `fastapi/applications.py` as well.
